text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM
- Egyptian President Mubarak and Gambian leader discuss the situation in Africa, international issues and bilateral ties.
- Pilgrimage council decides to cancel pilgrimage to Mecca with state funds.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Mubarak expected to meet on the fringes of the Davos World Economic Forum.
- State to sell 65,000 acres (26,325 hectares) of land in Sinai; will encourage investment in agricultural projects in the new valley.
- Minister of Religious Endowments Mahmoud Hamdi Zakzouk issues decree regulating the lectures and lessons at mosques.
- Sudanese opposition say they control 30 percent of southern and eastern Sudan.
- Cabinet to follow-up decisions taken last year in a meeting tomorrow.
AL-AKHBAR
- Mubarak, Gambian president discuss economic ties. Exports to increase and mutual investments to be encouraged.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa tells reporters that the Sudanese government has divided the Sudanese people. We will not stand with our hands tied if there is any foreign interference. We are following with interest Israeli actions in the Middle East.
- Investment Authority head Ibrahim Fawzi says new investment law will allow tax exemptions for new projects and that the government is considering not taxing projects in the new valley for 25 years.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Egyptian companies to take part in Gambian mega-projects.
- Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagui said the number of tourists visiting Egypt will rise to 6.2 million by the year 2000 which will mean a $5 billion increase in Egypt's income.
- Health Minister Ismail Sallam heads committee working to prevent the spread of any epidemic or work-related diseases in Toskha.
- Sheikh al-Azhar says satanists are not Moslems, Christians or Jews but members of the rich classes that have submerged themselves in vice.
- Education minister orders expulsion of satanists from school.
- Female satanists tell the prosecutor: We attended the parties and we drank the liquor but we are not devil worshippers and we did not have sex.
$1 = 3.4 Egyptian pounds
